# One row per hook surface the OpenCode adapter reaches, plus one row per canonical
# registration that has no OpenCode surface. Every registration in
# loader) is accounted for exactly once, by name, in the `reason` or `evidence` field of
# Schema (7 TAB-separated fields; a genuinely empty field collapses under IFS=tab read, so
# empty is never allowed — use the `-` sentinel):
#   bind                     — the plugin binds it and the canonical hook's decision is delivered
#   downgraded               — bound, but the canonical hook's contract is narrower here; the

#   already-covered-by-config — the config key delivers it, so no plugin binding is needed
#   absent-with-reason       — no OpenCode surface exists; the reason says why, never "manual"
# The binding column names the plugin call site, or `-` when nothing is bound.
# Load-bearing facts for every row below, all measured live on OpenCode 2.0.32 (measurement
# §6.6, §12): the V2 hook surface communicates only by mutating the event object it is handed,
# `ctx.event.subscribe` is a one-way iterator with no return channel, and so no hook can defer

column6: hooks/browser-snapshot-credential-guard.sh decides the call; a deny is written to event.effect with the reason in event.message, and the tool ends in permission.rejected carrying that reason to the model. A guard that exits non-zero with no parseable decision (missing or moved checkout, unresolved token, spawn error, timeout) is a deny naming the dead path — never an implicit allow, because a guard that did not run cannot vouch for the call
hooks/destructive-command-guard.sh is delivered without narrowing: a deny becomes effect=deny and an ask becomes effect=ask, the real prompt, so neither value is collapsed
column7: measurement §12.2 (deny blocks; ask holds the tool in `running`); plugins/soleur/opencode/plugin.ts decisionMessage()

column6: hooks/operator-stage-approval.sh needs a rewritten command AND an ask in the same decision (ADR-264). No single surface offers both: permission.evaluate can ask, but its `resources` is typed readonly and no rewrite ever reached the tool; tool.execute.before can rewrite `tool.input`, but its only refusal is a throw, which cannot prompt. Binding either half alone would consume an approval receipt on an unapproved write, i.e. a false approval — worse than absent

ctx.tool.hook("execute.before") is a real blocking surface, measured: a throw there ends the tool in error and the message reaches the model. It is deliberately NOT bound, because it fires BEFORE permission.evaluate, so a throw would preempt the true ask behind it and re-degrade every guard's ask into a refusal

The code-mode `execute` tool carries JavaScript in `input.code`, not a shell command string, so the Bash guards' input contract does not reach it. It also never fires permission.evaluate — a live call fired tool.execute.before with tool="execute" and no `command`, then no permission event — so a shell command issued from inside code mode is not decided here. Disclosed, not implied

The AGENTS.rules.md corpus (ADR-151) is injected into event.system on the first model request of a session. Where the repository carries .claude/hooks/session-rules-loader.sh it is invoked and its additionalContext used verbatim; otherwise the corpus is read directly with the two properties that must not be lost: a symlink is refused, and frontmatter is stripped

The canonical loader's additions are NOT reproduced on the direct-read path: the manifest, the tmpfs alarm block, the SOC 2 session-context snapshot, the over-strip guard, and the `(N of M rules)` stamp exist only when the canonical loader is present

The post-compaction re-read directive is ARMED by the compaction hook and injected on the next real request, rather than by resuming a stop — conditional on session.hook("context") firing, a fire §12.3 captured once and §14.0 records as unreconciled by a later probe (#10587), so no compaction-support claim is published from this row. hooks/compaction-state.sh's window/reset bookkeeping is not reproduced: it counts compact_boundary records in a Claude Code transcript, and this harness has no equivalent surface

hooks/stop-hook.sh and hooks/unkept-promise-hook.sh bind Stop. OpenCode V2 has no Stop hook and no member of its hook surface can defer a stop or force a continuation, so an unkept promise cannot be refused here; the completion marker is advisory and autonomous skills lean on their structural checks

Observation only by construction: session.* lifecycle events are recorded (advisory-completion-marker-not-enforceable) when SOLEUR_OPENCODE_EVENT_LOG names a path, and the subscriber has no return channel through which to act
hooks/codex-session-start.sh's plugin-root + INSTRUCTIONS stamp is delivered by the `instructions` key of the generated opencode.json fragment instead of by a hook

hooks/devin-session-start.sh is a Devin-only bootstrap: it is predicated on the Devin environment markers and instructs a Devin session about a Devin plugin payload. An OpenCode session takes the same boot context from the session-rules-loader injection bound above, so binding this script would be an inert double injection

hooks/welcome-hook.sh, hooks/version-banner.sh and hooks/ext-filter-detect.sh each emit a user-visible `systemMessage`. A plugin's setup() has no operator-facing message channel, and there is no session-start event to bind
